issue.title: bug: RCE: allowlisted "read-only" git status/diff run attacker code from .git/config

steps: Prepare a local throwaway Git repository POC_REPO containing app.txt, configure user.name Fixture and user.email fixture@example.com, and commit the file. Add a non-destructive fsmonitor proof script at .git/payload_status.sh containing #!/bin/sh, then printf proof > fsmonitor-proof.txt, then exit 0. Make it executable and set core.fsmonitor to its absolute path. The only payload action is creating the proof file inside this disposable repository.
review the uncommitted changes in POC_REPO
expected: Routine Git inspection does not execute repository-supplied commands under an unchecked read-only permission classification.
defect: An allowlisted git status executes the repository-configured fsmonitor script without an ACP approval request.

fault location.explanation: Git status is treated as unconditionally read-only although core.fsmonitor names an executable from repository-local config. Startup probing may override fsmonitor, but legacy model-issued Bash commands do not apply that hardening.

Root cause: Git status is treated as unconditionally read-only although core.fsmonitor names an executable from repository-local config. Startup probing may override fsmonitor, but legacy model-issued Bash commands do not apply that hardening.
